gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the price of reaching 10GbE on each 4-bay candidate. On the makers' US stores on 2026-11-08, the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus costs $619.99 with 10GbE built in. The QNAP TS-464-8G needs a $99 card on top of its $639, so it comes to $738. The Synology DS925+, which Fstoppers and Camera Lookout both name Best Overall, has no slot that can take 10GbE.
standout_why: Neither cited rival page has this. Fstoppers (best-nas-photographers-2026) prints one price, $1,299 at B&H for the QNAP TVS-h474, and no price for any other pick or add-in card. Camera Lookout (best-nas-systems-for-photographers) prints no prices at all. Both say the DS925+ has no 10GbE path and that the TS-464 and DS1825+ need a card, but neither puts a price on that card. ChatGPT's answers showed enclosure prices only ($619.99 for the DXP4800 Plus at B&H, $639 for the TS-464 and $829.99 or no price for the DS925+), never the cost to reach 10GbE.
decides: This backs the DXP4800 Plus as the pick for someone with a 10 TB RAW library who edits over the network. It is the cheapest 4-bay here with 10GbE built in, at $619.99. That is $19 below the TS-464 before the TS-464 even gets a 10GbE card, and $118 below it once the $99 card is added. The QXG-10G1TD card was also listed with a 2–4 week lead time. The DXP4800 GT costs $40 more ($659.99) and has two 10GbE ports. The DXP4800 Pro costs $180 more ($799.99), and Fstoppers says it is the same chassis with a faster CPU. The DS925+ only wins if the shopper edits from a local SSD and cares more about the software than 10GbE, because it can never go past 2.5GbE. TerraMaster's 5GbE F4-425 Pro ($629.99) and F4-425 Plus ($599.99) are the only models near this price, and they stop at 5GbE.
